title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use urgent language to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and payment details right now."
red_flags: Caller says your benefits will be canceled immediately
Asks for your Social Security number or bank info
Uses threats or pressure to act fast
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a number for help. If you call, scammers pretend to fix your computer and ask for money or access to your device.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-888-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up uses scary language about viruses
Gives a phone number to call right away
Asks for remote access or payment
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; use your own trusted tech support if you need help.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They may say there’s been an accident or arrest.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need bail money. Please don’t tell mom and dad. Send money now."
red_flags: Says there’s an emergency and needs money fast
Wants payment by gift card, wire transfer, or cash
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check if the story is true.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link to fix it. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or asks for payment.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to confirm your address: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to a website you don’t recognize
Asks for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Do not click the link; check your real delivery status by going to the official website or app.

title: Social Security Suspension Scam
how_it_works: Scammers call or email saying your Social Security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity. They ask you to confirm your number or pay to reactivate it.
example_message: "This is the Social Security Administration. Your number has been suspended. Press 1 to speak to an agent or your benefits will stop."
red_flags: Threatens to suspend your Social Security number
Asks for your number or payment
what_to_do: Do not respond; contact Social Security directly using the official number if you have concerns.
